A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Universal Beta Splatting. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original UBS rendering-quality and efficiency results, component ablations, and rotation-parameterization experiments in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds UBS results on real-world N3V videos and a primitive-capacity study in Tables 5 and 9.

M1.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 substantively revise the stated procedure: diag(s_q) becomes L_q in the covariance factor, conditioning Beta weights acquire a bound of 1, and opacity uses squared Cholesky-whitened residuals instead of inverse-covariance residuals followed by max(tanh(d_raw/2),0). These are non-equivalent computational definitions, although the PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: V2 adds six-scene N3V evaluation on real-world dynamic videos in Appendix A.1, Table 5. This extends dynamic coverage beyond v1's synthetic and physically based D-NeRF and 7DGS-PBR scenes. All five original benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: V2 Table 4 adds DRKS, Textured GS, Quadratic GS, and Disc-GS to the static comparison previously in v1 Table 3. Its new N3V comparison also includes Ex4DGS and 4DGaussians (Wu et al.), previously absent from reported comparisons, alongside 4DGS and 7DGS. The evaluated comparator set therefore broadens substantially.

E3.justification: V2 introduces controlled 100K, 200K, and 300K primitive capacities in Table 9 and adds storage size and primitive count to quantitative evaluation. The previously stated 30K-iteration training, learning rates, hardware, dynamic batch size, and final-iteration reporting remain unchanged. N3V-specific protocol details are not supplied.

E4.justification: Table 9 and Appendix B.2 add a sensitivity analysis testing reconstruction quality, rendering speed, and storage across primitive capacities on NeRF Synthetic. The existing component/CUDA ablation and rotation-parameterization study retain their results, moving from v1 Tables 2 and 6 to v2 Tables 3 and 10.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, explicit seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional tables continue reporting point estimates and averages across scenes, without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V2 adds N3V results, including UBS-7D's reported 32.22 dB average versus Ex4DGS's 32.11 dB, additional static-baseline scores, extensive efficiency results, and capacity-study outcomes. Main Table 1 and existing ablation scores remain unchanged apart from equivalent rounding. Removing LPIPS columns from the 6DGS-PBR appendix table loses DBS results; the corresponding 3DGS, 6DGS, and UBS values remain in Table 1.

T1.justification: The conditioning-weight domain and opacity-distance definition are revised. Appendix C.1 additionally derives the covariance blocks and develops the skew-symmetric rotation construction, explicitly qualifying first-order orthogonality as approximate for small rotation norms. The earlier Beta-kernel shape and Gaussian-approximation properties remain, so the theoretical development largely refines the existing framework.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same substantive claims: unified multidimensional Beta primitives, no auxiliary appearance networks, interpretable decomposition, approximate Gaussian compatibility, and quality/efficiency benefits. The headline improvements and claimed performance lower bounds are unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 interprets N3V results as evidence of applicability to real-world temporal and appearance variation. Appendix B.2 newly explains how MCMC capacity control supports practical speed-quality tradeoffs, while Appendix C.1 qualifies approximate orthogonality. Existing explanations of Gaussian limitations and scene decomposition remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 newly discloses per-scene primitive counts and storage sizes and specifies zero initialization of rotation parameters in Appendix C.1. Core training details and the project link remain unchanged. It also removes v1 Table 3's explicit statement that available baseline values come from the original papers, reducing result-provenance information.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands the alternative-kernel discussion with TNT-GS, Quadratic GS, Half-Gaussian Splatting, Disc-GS, Textured Gaussians, Triangle Splatting, and DRKS, distinguishing kernel-shape, appearance, and geometric-primitive approaches from multidimensional UBS. N3V and Ex4DGS references are also added. Publication-status updates to existing references do not constitute new cited works.

P1.justification: V2 expands the preliminary rendering explanations, rewrites the alternative-kernel paragraph, makes local wording corrections, and reorganizes the appendices into comparisons, efficiency, and parameterization subsections. Most introductory, experimental, and concluding prose remains intact; this is a localized editorial revision rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: V2 adds separate aggregate-efficiency, per-scene-efficiency, N3V-comparison, and capacity-study tables. It expands the static comparison, removes LPIPS columns from the appendix PBR table, and rearranges retained tables. These substantially expand the quantitative presentation; all four figures retain their image content.

improvement.justification: The real-world dynamic evaluation and model-level efficiency/capacity results provide useful evidence missing from v1, making applicability and computational tradeoffs easier to assess. The net gain is limited by sparse N3V protocol documentation, lost DBS LPIPS and baseline-provenance information, and the revised opacity definition in Equation 11 remaining unreconciled with the earlier distance formula retained in Appendix D.
